title: The one line, and selling winners without fear
objectives: Use the one line to answer any rebalancing pushback.
Explain why trimming winners is not abandoning equity.
body_md:
The one line to remember: rebalancing is a promise kept to the client's own risk choice. Trimming equity back to 60% is not abandoning equity — the client still holds 60% in equity. Buying debt after a fall is not “putting money into something falling” — it is following the rule agreed while things were calm, buying at lower prices without guessing the bottom. Debt earns its place in bad years: it is what we use to buy equity after a fall.

> **Investor takeaway:** Rebalancing is a promise kept to the client's own risk choice.
example: “Why put more into something that's falling?” → “This is the rule we agreed while things were calm. It buys at lower prices, without guessing the bottom.”
say: We're only trimming back to the mix you chose.
Debt is what we use to buy equity after a fall.
never: Debt earns no place in a portfolio.

check.q: Arun's funds look 80% equity, but he has ₹30 L in PPF and FDs. What do you do?
o: Measure drift on the whole portfolio; his total mix may already be near target
check.why: Measure drift on the whole portfolio; his total mix may already be near target.

check.q: What is the one line to remember in this module?
o: Rebalancing is a promise kept to the client's own risk choice
check.why: The one line to remember: rebalancing is a promise kept to the client's own risk choice.

check.q: “Debt has done nothing; let's drop it” is best answered:
o: “Debt is what we use to buy equity after a fall. It earns its place in bad years.”
check.why: Recency bias: “Debt has done nothing; let's drop it.” Say: “Debt is what we use to buy equity after a fall. It earns its place in bad years.”
